claims.text: A DeepMD-like MLIP can be trained on ab initio configurations covering both liquid and solid high-entropy carbonitride phases.
The proposed MLIP training set is extensive and represents diverse solid and liquid configurations.
Replacing conventional EAM references with a liquid–solid-trained MLIP will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved reference–target overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Conventional EAM potentials cannot capture the full diversity of ab initio liquid configurations in these high-entropy alloys.
Current TOR-TILD approaches use conventional EAM potentials as reference systems.
Deep-learning MLIPs capture many-body interactions and subtle local atomic environments that EAM potentials miss.
A liquid–solid-trained DeepMD potential accurately represents the energies of both ordered and disordered configurations in the considered high-entropy carbonitride system.
Accurate reproduction of the near-melting energy landscape bridges the configurational gap between the ab initio target and the simulation reference.
The method applies to complex multicomponent alloys over approximately 0.9–1.1 times their melting temperature.
Near melting, liquid and solid configurations in these alloys are highly diverse.
The MLIP intervention will produce a statistically significant decrease in thermodynamic-integration error relative to EAM references.
Reducing integration-path mismatch will improve the reliability of free-energy and melting-temperature estimates.
The intervention should be most effective in alloys with complex many-body interactions and broad distributions of configurations near melting.
The intervention's effectiveness in simpler alloys or at lower temperatures remains untested.
Cumulative integration error can be used to quantify thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
